title: Permutation invariance of product means
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability distribution on $\Omega$, let $n$ be a natural number, let $\sigma$ be a permutation of the $n$ coordinates, and let $h:(\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\Omega)\to\mathbb R$. The product mean of the function obtained by permuting the input coordinates according to $\sigma$ equals the product mean of $h$.
hypotheses_covered: $\sigma$ is a permutation of the $n$ coordinates
$h$ is a real-valued function on length-$n$ sequences from $\Omega$
